ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Rock climbing is a form of sport that tests people's will and psychological quality; outdoor rock climbing is even more exciting and thrilling. As shown in the figure, it is a scene and movement route diagram of outdoor rock climbing. This rock climbing enthusiast goes from the starting point a to b, and finally reaches c. Based on this figure, judge which of the following statements is correct (　　)
A. The route abc in the figure represents the displacement traveled by the rock climbing enthusiast
B. The distance traveled by the rock climbing enthusiast is greater than the displacement from the starting point to the endpoint
C. The total length of the route traveled by the rock climbing enthusiast from the starting point to the endpoint is equal to the displacement
D. The ratio of the total route length to the time taken by the rock climbing enthusiast is equal to his average velocity

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left side of the figure shows a scene of a climber climbing on a rock wall; the right side is a schematic diagram of the rock climbing route, marked with starting point a, intermediate point b, and endpoint c. The route starts from the lower point a, follows a bent and detouring curve through b, and finally reaches the higher point c; it is not a straight line from a to c. Reasoning: The climber actually follows the curve from a through b to c, and the length of this curve represents the distance he traveled; the magnitude of the displacement from starting point a to endpoint c is the straight-line distance between points a and c. Since the straight line between two points is the shortest, and the actual route shown has obvious bends, the actual distance is greater than the magnitude of the displacement from the starting point to the endpoint. Final answer: The distance traveled by the rock climbing enthusiast is greater than the magnitude of the displacement from starting point a to endpoint c.
